mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline by the specified thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4% for three consecutive months indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained unemployment above 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% on a 3-month moving average, combined with a concurrent drop in retail sales (RSAFS), signals supply chain and demand contraction pressures, which drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both INDPRO and RSAFS meet the specified triggers.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month decline in the federal funds rate below 2% signals an emergency monetary easing in response to financial stress, which boosts risk appetite and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops by > 0.75pp in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS drops > 0.75pp in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in the unemployment rate and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% month-over-month indicate a rapidly deteriorating labor market, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases AND PAYEMS decreases > 1% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls by > 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annual increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 6% for four consecutive months signals entrenched inflation, which leads the Federal Reserve to maintain restrictive policy and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained CPIAUCSL > 6% for four months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) of more than 1% signals broad-based contraction in economic activity, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of the monetary policy stance.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both INDPRO and HOUST decline by > 1% in the same month.
